nonogram.q1: How do you solve a nonogram?
nonogram.a1: The numbers beside each row and above each column give the lengths of the filled blocks in that line, in order, with at least one empty cell between blocks. Fill cells that must be part of a block, cross out cells that must stay empty, and the picture appears.
nonogram.a2: The whole row or column is empty. You can cross out all of its cells at once by dragging along it in cross mode.
nonogram.q3: Do I ever have to guess?
nonogram.a3: No. Each puzzle here is checked when it is made: it has exactly one solution, and you can always find the next cell by looking at one row or column at a time.
nonogram.q4: How do I mark a cell as empty?
nonogram.a4: Right-click it, press and hold on a touch screen, or turn on Cross mode. Crosses are only notes; they do not count for or against you.
nonogram.q5: Are nonograms the same as griddlers or paint by numbers?
nonogram.a5: Yes. Nonograms are also called griddlers, hanjie, paint by numbers or picture logic puzzles.

memory-game.q1: How do you play the memory game?
memory-game.a1: All cards start face down. Turn over two: if they show the same picture they stay up, otherwise they turn back. Remember where each picture was and clear the board in as few moves as you can.
memory-game.a2: Players take turns. Finding a pair scores a point and lets the same player go again; a miss passes the turn. The player with more pairs wins.
memory-game.a3: Turning over two cards is one move. Your best result for each board size is the fewest moves you needed.
memory-game.q4: Can I tell the cards apart without colour?
memory-game.a4: Yes. Every picture is a different shape or a solid shape against an outlined one, and the two colours differ strongly in lightness.
memory-game.a5: It is a classic concentration game for children and adults. Start with 4×4 and move to 6×6 when it gets easy.

nonogram.lead: Solve a nonogram in three steps.
nonogram.s1b: Choose 5×5, 10×10 or 15×15. A first visit opens a small puzzle; tap New puzzle for another.
nonogram.s2b: Each number is a block of filled cells in that row or column, in order. Fill what must be filled and cross out what must stay empty.
nonogram.s3b: When every row and column matches its clues, the picture is complete. Turn on Check mistakes if you are stuck.

memory-game.lead: Play the memory game in three steps.
memory-game.s1b: Pick 4×4, 4×5 or 6×6 and one or two players.
memory-game.s2b: Tap two cards. A matching pair stays face up; other cards turn back.
memory-game.s3b: Find every pair. Fewer moves is better; with two players, more pairs wins.
